summary: The second revision of the BBN schedule for adding core memory to IMPs and TIPs. Retrofits at several sites were completed and removed, and others were rescheduled. It restates the text of RFC 447.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC revises the schedule for memory upgrades to IMPs and TIPs. It removes completed sites and lists remaining dates and expected memory sizes.

questions: how much memory did a tip have in 1973
subtitle: A revised schedule for adding core memory to ARPANET IMPs and TIPs.

tldr.problem: BBN needed to coordinate memory retrofits at IMP and TIP sites while limiting disruption to users.
tldr.mechanism: The revision removes sites whose retrofits were complete, reschedules others, and lists remaining retrofit dates and resulting memory sizes.
tldr.outcome: RFC 476 obsoletes RFC 447 and is a dated operational schedule for 1973.

today: RFC 476 obsoletes RFC 447. It is a historical schedule for the 1973 IMP/TIP memory retrofit program.

sections.title: What Revision 2 Changes
sections.content:
RFC 476 revises the schedule in RFC 447. It removes Utah, Belvoir, NOAA, USC, Stanford, ISI, Case and CCA because their retrofits were completed, and reschedules UCSB, ETAC, Aberdeen and Rome.

The RFC reproduces the revised text of RFC 447 for the remaining work.
sections.plainLanguage: Completed sites are removed from the schedule. Several other sites receive new dates.

sections.title: Memory After the Retrofit
sections.content:
The plan is to add core memory to IMPs and TIPs during the first several months of 1973. At completion, an IMP (516 or 316) is listed at 16K words, a TIP at 28K words, and a TIP with Magnetic Tape Option at 32K words.

The expansion of TIP core memory requires two cabinets. The RFC asks sites anticipating floor-space difficulties to contact BBN.
sections.plainLanguage: The planned memory sizes are 16K words for an IMP, 28K for a TIP and 32K for a TIP with Magnetic Tape Option. The expanded TIP occupies two cabinets.

sections.title: Scheduling the Work
sections.content:
The schedule is arranged to coincide with usual monthly Preventive Maintenance at each site, to minimize user inconvenience. The work may keep machines down longer than normal. Dates are given as month and day.

Aberdeen is listed as postponed indefinitely, and the author says further RFCs will update the schedule if necessary.
sections.plainLanguage: The work is planned alongside regular maintenance, but machines may be unavailable for longer than usual. Aberdeen has no new date in this revision.

references.text: McKenzie, A., "IMP/TIP Memory Retrofit Schedule", RFC 447.
